# r2 — Discoverable

## What this measures

Can an agent *find out* that this site does commerce, and which protocols it
speaks? Each protocol defines a well-known discovery document; publishing one
is the cheapest, highest-leverage readiness move there is (complexity 1,
impact 5 — top of the priority formula).

## Sub-checks

| Sub-check | Pass when | Weight | Fix skill |
|-----------|-----------|-------:|-----------|
| UCP profile | `GET /.well-known/ucp` (or `.json`) → 200 JSON declaring `services`/`capabilities` | 2 | `ucp-agentic-commerce:ucp-setup` |
| ACP discovery doc | `GET /.well-known/acp.json` (or `/agentic-commerce`) → 200 JSON with `protocol.name=="acp"` or `api_base_url` | 2 | `acp-agentic-commerce:acp-setup` |
| A2A agent card | `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` → 200 JSON with card fields | 1 | `a2a-multi-agent:a2a-agent-card` |
| llms.txt | `GET /llms.txt` → 200, > 40 bytes | 1 | `nlweb-protocol:nlweb-schema-org-grounding` |
| sitemap.xml | `GET /sitemap.xml` → 200 with `<urlset>`/`<sitemapindex>` | 1 | — |
| product feed | `GET /feeds/products.xml` (or `.tsv`) → 200, ≥ 1 KB, non-HTML content-type (a SPA catch-all serving index.html does not count) | 1 | `acp-agentic-commerce:acp-product-feed` |

## N/A condition

None — discovery applies to any site that wants agents as customers.

## Fix guidance

One protocol done well beats three stubs: pick the platform your buyers'
agents actually use, publish its discovery doc first, then broaden.
A Shopify storefront gets `/.well-known/ucp` from the platform — verify it
resolves on the *storefront domain*, not just the myshopify.com host.
